config._doc: The three vLLM cells phase 0 could not measure, re-declared so they fit and re-run. #354. Each refused on an EMPTY card with torch.OutOfMemoryError inside _allocate_kv_cache, and in each the declared KV bytes were exactly what the entry's own shape computes -- the rule was right and produced a figure the card cannot hold. THE DECLARATION HAS CHANGED, which is why this is a separate campaign and not a re-run of phase 0: max_num_seqs stays at the campaign's 8 and max_model_len is shortened until the entry fits, chosen by the owner 2026-08-23 over the other way out (holding 8192 and narrowing the width). Both reach the same KV bytes; they differ in what the server can then serve. The footprint these cells report is therefore the footprint OF THIS DECLARATION and is not comparable with phase 0's other vLLM rows.
config._supersedes_nothing: The phase-0 journal's three refused rows stand as measured. This campaign adds rows; it does not replace them, and neither table is the other's re-measurement.
config._headroom: Each entry was checked against vllm.declaration_fits before any rig time was spent, at the free memory both rigs read at rest (6,143 and 12,287 MiB). Slack after weights + KV + NON_KV_OVERHEAD_MIB: srv1/4B 369 MiB, srv2/4B 753 MiB, srv2/14B 235 MiB. The 14B's margin is under one 256 MiB allocator block and it is run at that declaration deliberately: if it refuses, the engine's own words say whether NON_KV_OVERHEAD_MIB needs a term that grows with the model, which is a fact worth one cell.

identity_refusals.concurrency: `max_num_seqs` — the scheduler's batch width, which is what this field means — is not on vLLM 0.26.0's HTTP surface. Searched exhaustively on 2026-08-18: every parameterless GET in the server's own /openapi.json route table (11 answered) on srv1 and srv2, including /server_info's full engine config, all 122 /metrics series, and /v1/models. `vllm:cache_config_info.kv_cache_max_concurrency` looks like the answer and is NOT: it is KV-cache capacity, and it moves opposite to the flag — srv1 ran --max-num-seqs 8 and reported 16.004, srv2 ran 16 and reported 5.314. It is not unknowable, only unaskable: a concurrency ramp recovers it, and on srv1 it read the knee at exactly 8 — throughput plateauing at 106.5 tok/s and per-request latency flat at ~9.5s through n=8 before the queue forms. That is a measurement this capture must not make, because it would perturb the run it describes. The raw metrics are under native

identity_refusals.concurrency: `max_num_seqs` — the scheduler's batch width, which is what this field means — is not on vLLM 0.26.0's HTTP surface. Searched exhaustively on 2026-08-18: every parameterless GET in the server's own /openapi.json route table (11 answered) on srv1 and srv2, including /server_info's full engine config, all 122 /metrics series, and /v1/models. `vllm:cache_config_info.kv_cache_max_concurrency` looks like the answer and is NOT: it is KV-cache capacity, and it moves opposite to the flag — srv1 ran --max-num-seqs 8 and reported 16.004, srv2 ran 16 and reported 5.314. It is not unknowable, only unaskable: a concurrency ramp recovers it, and on srv1 it read the knee at exactly 8 — throughput plateauing at 106.5 tok/s and per-request latency flat at ~9.5s through n=8 before the queue forms.
